parameters.name: Freshness bound
parameters.description: How recent the last accepted header must be before release. A multiple of BSV block time — ~1,500 Solana slots per block. Implemented (StaleClient), untested on a local validator
parameters.doc_description: How recent the last accepted header must be before release. A multiple of BSV block time — ~1,500 Solana slots per block. **Implemented (`StaleClient`), untested on a local validator**

parameters.name: Maturity
parameters.description: How deep a deposit's block must be before its staged mint releases, in BSV blocks. 144 blocks is about 24 hours at BSV's 600 s target. This is the window in which a reorg is caught and the mint burned. Constraint: confirmations + maturity <= window, so 12 + 144 <= 192. SET TO 144: at 0 the mint side had no window at all, and an affordable rented reorg could not be reversed.
parameters.doc_description: Staged mints wait this long before release. **A stored parameter, not a constant**, so governance can raise it without a redeploy. At 0 the vault is a pass-through and release/burn are a **race**. The designed value is **144 blocks**

parameters.name: Detection margin
parameters.description: window − maturity. Do not add floor into this subtraction. Zero at the maximum committed depth
parameters.csv_value: %v% blocks at the designed values der
parameters.doc_description: `window − maturity`. **Do not add `floor` into this subtraction.** Zero at the maximum committed depth

parameters.name: Rent refund on close
parameters.description: Closing an item returns its rent to the caller
parameters.doc_description: Closing an item returns its rent to the caller

parameters.name: Mint-side bond — BSV side (the float)
parameters.description: Held outside the reserve. The bond is the float — working capital for transfers — not a capital requirement sized against the reserve, and not a capacity ceiling. The k × (BSV held) line is a solvency check on mint and exit. Held under the collective (threshold ECDSA) key, not the member's own, and seized by the members collectively; slashing pays the slashers from it. A collective action by the majority, not an automatic rule
parameters.doc_description: Held **outside the reserve**. **The bond is the float** — working capital for transfers — **not a capital requirement sized against the reserve**, and not a capacity ceiling. The `k × (BSV held)` line is a solvency check on mint and exit. **Held under the collective (threshold ECDSA) key, not the member's own**, and seized by the **members collectively**; slashing pays the slashers from it. A collective action by the majority, not an automatic rule

parameters.name: Mint-side bond custody
parameters.description: The design requirement the mechanism rests on. If a member controls their own bond they move it the moment they are caught. Residuals: a majority could seize an honest member's bond; nothing on BSV compels signing, so the duty to slash is social
parameters.doc_description: **The design requirement the mechanism rests on.** If a member controls their own bond they move it the moment they are caught. *Residuals:* a majority could seize an honest member's bond; nothing on BSV compels signing, so the duty to slash is **social**

parameters.name: Redeem-side bond — solBSV side (the float)
parameters.description: Seizable on Solana. This side is enforceable. Neither bond sits inside the reserve
parameters.doc_description: Seizable on Solana. **This side is enforceable.** Neither bond sits inside the reserve

parameters.name: Nominal bond size
parameters.description: Superseded by the two side-specific bonds; kept as the per-side default name
parameters.doc_description: Superseded by the two side-specific bonds; kept as the per-side default name

parameters.name: Aggregate bond (tracked)
parameters.description: The old single running total is replaced by two side-specific aggregates
parameters.doc_description: The old single running total is replaced by two side-specific aggregates

parameters.name: Bonds gate minting
parameters.description: F5. A mint is refused unless the BSV-side bond covers the BSV held after it. A solvency floor, not a capacity claim. The old total_bond ≥ k × (non_bonded_supply + amount) is superseded
parameters.doc_description: **F5.** A mint is refused unless the BSV-side bond covers the BSV held after it. A **solvency floor, not a capacity claim.** The old `total_bond ≥ k × (non_bonded_supply + amount)` is **superseded**

parameters.name: Bond denomination
parameters.description: Mint side BSV, redeem side solBSV; neither inside the reserve. No price oracle is needed for either
parameters.doc_description: Mint side BSV, redeem side `solBSV`; neither inside the reserve. No price oracle is needed for either

parameters.name: Against a colluding threshold
parameters.description: Stated risk, not a mechanism. No on-chain predicate proves who signed an off-chain threshold signature. The maximum loss is the whole non-member supply. Publishing the reserve and supply converts a hidden theft into a visible one; the unchallenged-spend case is separately addressed by the reported spent-outpoint record
parameters.doc_description: **Stated risk, not a mechanism.** No on-chain predicate proves who signed an off-chain threshold signature. The maximum loss is the whole **non-member supply**. Publishing the reserve and supply converts a hidden theft into a visible one; the unchallenged-spend case is separately addressed by the **reported spent-outpoint record**

parameters.name: Bond coverage floor
parameters.description: bsv_bond ≥ k × (BSV held) and solbsv_bond ≥ k × (solBSV held), checked on mint and exit. A solvency check, not a capacity ceiling. The capacity arithmetic built on k and n/t is withdrawn. Capital inefficiency accepted
parameters.doc_description: `bsv_bond ≥ k × (BSV held)` and `solbsv_bond ≥ k × (solBSV held)`, checked on mint and exit. **A solvency check, not a capacity ceiling.** The capacity arithmetic built on `k` and `n/t` is **withdrawn**. Capital inefficiency accepted

parameters.name: Gateway signing threshold
parameters.description: t of n for the gateway threshold ECDSA key. N is a variable; the number is arbitrary and deferred. The key emits one signature and is one leg of the reserve's 2-of-2 script. Changing t or n is a re-sharing, not a migration
parameters.doc_description: `t` of `n` for the gateway **threshold ECDSA** key. **`N` is a variable; the number is arbitrary and deferred.** The key emits **one** signature and is one leg of the reserve's 2-of-2 script. Changing `t` or `n` is a **re-sharing**, not a migration

parameters.name: Greycore size
parameters.description: The second signer set on the reserve script: trusted third parties, not node operators — people with reputations to lose, who do not run the reserve. The Greycore finds and admits replacement members
parameters.doc_description: The second signer set on the reserve script: **trusted third parties, not node operators** — people with reputations to lose, who do not run the reserve. The Greycore **finds and admits replacement members**

parameters.name: Greycore threshold
parameters.description: How many Greycore keys must sign alongside the gateway. The Greycore co-signs every reserve spend, which is what constrains the reserve. 4-of-5 was an earlier proposal and is not settled
parameters.doc_description: How many Greycore keys must sign alongside the gateway. The Greycore **co-signs every reserve spend**, which is what constrains the reserve. 4-of-5 was an earlier proposal and is not settled

parameters.name: Shard count

parameters.doc_description: One key or several groups. Affects blast radius and latency. **There is no sharding today: blast radius is 100%**

parameters.doc_description: `OP_2 <gateway threshold key> <greycore key> OP_2 OP_CHECKMULTISIG`. Both keys must sign; the Greycore polices every reserve spend. The signer is the upgrade authority — a PoC stand-in for the federation, which does not exist yet. Permanent and rent-exempt with no prune: closing a record would re-open the mint of an already-spent deposit
parameters.doc_value: **one PDA per `(txid, vout)`, written by the program authority**

The signer is the **upgrade authority** — a **PoC stand-in** for the federation, which does not exist yet. parameters.name: Minimum delay (floor)
parameters.description: F7. Both readings are defensible and the choice is open: with a floor, a majority cannot take the warning away — proposal 1 can only shorten the delay to the floor, so proposal 2 still has to be exited during it; without, the exit window is whatever the current majority allows. A judgement about trust, not a correctness question
parameters.doc_description: **F7.** Both readings are defensible and the choice is open: *with a floor*, a majority cannot take the warning away — proposal 1 can only shorten the delay to the floor, so proposal 2 still has to be exited during it; *without*, the exit window is whatever the current majority allows. A judgement about trust, **not a correctness question**

parameters.name: Redemption deadline
parameters.description: How long a member has to pay before the holder may cancel. In Solana SLOTS, because a height deadline would never expire if the header feed stalled. NOTE: the earlier claim that this must exceed payout_confirmations + challenge_window does NOT hold at these values (216,000 slots against 150 BSV blocks). The pay-and-refund race is closed structurally instead -- cancel_redeem is refused while a claim is live.
parameters.doc_description: `D`. In Solana SLOTS, because a height deadline would never expire if the feed stalled. The earlier claim that `D ≥ payout_confirmations + challenge_window` **does not hold** at these values (216,000 slots against 150 BSV blocks); the pay-and-refund race is closed structurally instead — `cancel_redeem` is refused while a claim is live. A **stored, timelock-mutable `Config` field**, like `v.maturity_blocks`

parameters.name: Cancellation grace
parameters.description: Cancellation is immediate on expiry. A grace period would only delay the exit
parameters.doc_description: Cancellation is immediate on expiry. A grace period would only delay the exit

parameters.name: Minimum redemption

parameters.doc_description: Minimum redemption, so a claim's proof is worth the transaction fees to settle

parameters.doc_description: Cap on concurrent pending redemptions, so the escrow cannot be used to make the program's per-instruction work unbounded

sections.heading: ## Measured constants — do not change without re-measuring

status.name: built-mutable
status.meaning: In the program, in a runtime account, changeable through the timelocked authority

status.name: built-frozen
status.meaning: In the program as a compiled constant; changing it needs a **redeploy**

status.name: built-shape
status.meaning: The shape is enforced by the built program; the keys (or the authority) behind it are not

status.name: designed
status.meaning: **Not in the program.** A specification row: decided policy, an external measurement, or a derived quantity the program does not carry

status.name: open
status.meaning: **No value yet.** This is work to do, not a decision deferred

provenance.name: measured
provenance.meaning: From the chain, the code or the toolchain. Do not change without re-measuring

provenance.name: placeholder
provenance.meaning: A starting value — or no value yet — expected to move

provenance.name: derived
provenance.meaning: Computed from other parameters; changing it directly is a bug
